data.name: Rules_P_interval_Effect
data.value: 0 counts every advertisement; above 0, one reading every this many ms, repeating the previous one if nothing new arrived

data.name: Rules_P_lock_Effect
data.value: Readings below it count as "away"; while the lock prompt shows, readings above it mean "you came back"

data.value: Maximum wait for the sign-in result after sending the credentials

data.name: Rules_P_ucount_Effect
data.value: Used to unlock after locking (threshold {unlock}) and to withdraw the prompt (threshold {lock})

data.name: Rules_P_unlock_Effect
data.value: After locking, readings must be above it to count as "near, OK to unlock"

data.name: Rules_S0_Lead
data.value: These are the values the service is using. Any value that differs from the default shows the default next to it.{guardnote}

data.name: Rules_S1_I1_V
data.value: the address matches the identity address in the configuration, or the IRK resolves its random address.

data.name: Rules_S1_I2_V
data.value: -127 and below, +127 and above (including -128) mean "not measurable" and are dropped.

data.name: Rules_S1_I3_V
data.value: when above 0, counted readings are at least this far apart; now {interval} ms.

data.name: Rules_S1_I4_V
data.value: the service evaluates once per second, only on readings that arrived since the last check; readings are kept for up to 120 s.

data.name: Rules_S2_I1_V
data.value: a first reading past the threshold starts a batch and does not count itself.

data.name: Rules_S2_I2_V
data.value: N more readings follow, and every one must be past the threshold.

data.name: Rules_S2_I3_V
data.value: one reading that fails discards the whole batch; counting restarts at the next trigger.

data.name: Rules_S2_I4_V
data.value: strictly below {lock} ({lock} itself does not count).

data.name: Rules_S2_I5_V
data.value: strictly above the threshold. Withdrawing the prompt uses {lock}, with no limit on the gap between readings; automatic unlock uses {unlock}, at most 3 s between readings.

data.name: Rules_S2_I6_V
data.value: gaps up to 3 s are not evidence. After that, one -127 silence value per second joins the departure batch only if the last 2 readings in a row were already below {lock}{nosignal}. A single stray low reading does not count.

data.name: Rules_S2_I7_V
data.value: Every state change clears the batch in progress.

data.name: Rules_S2_Title
data.value: Core rule: the whole batch must pass

data.name: Rules_S3_I1_V
data.value: more than {grace} s since the service started or the PC woke;

data.name: Rules_S3_I2_V
data.value: the target device has been seen at least once since the service started;

data.name: Rules_S3_I3_V
data.value: a trigger reading below {lock} (or a silence trigger);

data.name: Rules_S3_I4_V
data.value: then {prompt} readings in a row below {lock} (silence values count).

data.name: Rules_S3_Lead
data.value: It moves to "About to lock" when all of these hold:

data.name: Rules_S4_I1_V
data.value: the dialog reaching its own display limit (the state stays "About to lock"); changing the target device.

data.name: Rules_S4_I2_V
data.value: readings are ignored; when the time is up it returns to Unlocked and section 3 starts over.

data.name: Rules_S4_I3_V
data.value: withdraw the prompt, ask the helper to lock; if it does not confirm in time, use the system command.

data.name: Rules_S4_Lead
data.value: The prompt never times out. In evaluation order, any of these ends it:

data.name: Rules_S4_R1_V
data.value: a trigger above {lock}, then {ucount} readings in a row above {lock}. Any gap between readings is fine: a watch may advertise only every ten seconds or so.

data.name: Rules_S4_R2_Res
data.value: Prompt withdrawn, screen locked → Locked · waiting

data.name: Rules_S4_R2_V
data.value: after the prompt appears, {confirm} new readings in a row below {lock} (silence values count); no trigger needed.

data.name: Rules_S4_R3_V
data.value: "Reject" pauses {reject} s; "Don't lock for {snooze} min" pauses {snooze} min; closing with × locks right away. A notification hidden by Windows (Do not disturb, full-screen app) is not a ×: it does not lock and asks again with a dialog.

data.name: Rules_S4_R5_V
data.value: the user never saw the prompt.

data.name: Rules_S4_R6_V
data.value: the user name or password in the configuration was changed to a wrong one and failed the check after reload.

data.name: Rules_S4_R7_V
data.value: very rare; only after a lock the service missed.

data.name: Rules_S4_Title
data.value: About to lock → prompt withdrawn, or locked

data.name: Rules_S5_I1_V
data.value: no credentials are sent in this state, however strong the signal;

data.name: Rules_S5_I2_V
data.value: past the {grace} s grace, a trigger below {lock}, then {prompt} readings in a row below {lock} (silence values count).

data.name: Rules_S5_Lead
data.value: After Win+L you must really leave once before automatic unlock is possible.

data.name: Rules_S6_I1_V
data.value: a trigger above {unlock}, then {ucount} readings in a row above {unlock}, at most 3 s apart; then the credentials are sent. Signals between {lock} and {unlock} never unlock.

data.name: Rules_S6_I2_V
data.value: the credential provider on the lock screen is connected; there have not been 3 sends in a row without a result (reset by a manual unlock or new credentials).

data.name: Rules_S6_I3_V
data.value: success → Unlocked; wrong, expired or must-change password, or locked account → Suspended with a notification; any other failure, or no result within {timeout} s → back to monitoring and retry.

data.name: Rules_S7_I1_V
data.value: everything except Suspended returns to Unlocked and resets the send counter.

data.name: Rules_S7_I2_V
data.value: everything except Suspended goes to Locked · waiting; a showing prompt is withdrawn first.

data.name: Rules_S7_I3_V
data.value: reading history is cleared, the {grace} s grace starts again, batches in progress are discarded.

data.name: Rules_S7_I4_V
data.value: goes to Suspended with a notification; a showing prompt is withdrawn first.

data.name: Rules_S7_I5_V
data.value: ignores readings and lock/unlock events; it resumes only after correct credentials pass the check.

data.name: Rules_S7_I6_V
data.value: If no advertisement from any device arrives for 30 s, silence no longer counts as leaving: the prompt is withdrawn, an armed unlock must confirm departure again, and BleUnlock restarts the scan, then the adapter, and notifies you.

data.name: Rules_S8_B1_1
data.value: You get up and leave; the reading drops to {trig}: that is the trigger and does not count.

data.name: Rules_S8_B1_2
data.value: The next {prompt} readings are all below {lock} → the prompt appears.

data.name: Rules_S8_B1_3
data.value: {confirm} more readings below {lock} after the prompt (one silence value per second once the signal is gone) → the screen locks.

data.name: Rules_S8_B1_4
data.value: Still no signal; {prompt} more silence values → ready to unlock.

data.name: Rules_S8_B1_5
data.value: You come back; the reading rises to {back}: trigger. The next {ucount} are above {unlock} → credentials are sent.

data.name: Rules_S8_B1_Title
data.value: Leave, lock, come back and unlock

data.name: Rules_S8_B2_1
data.value: The prompt is showing; you walk back a little and the reading returns to {w1}: that is the trigger.

data.name: Rules_S8_B2_2
data.value: The next {ucount} readings are above {lock} (for example {w2}, {w3}, {w4}) → the prompt is withdrawn and it returns to Unlocked without locking.

data.name: Rules_S8_B2_Title
data.value: The prompt appears, then you come back

data.name: MacRisk_Title
data.value: Security notice: MAC addresses are easy to spoof

data.name: MacRisk_Message
data.value: When tracking by MAC address, the PC recognises the device only by the address in its broadcasts. That address is broadcast in the open: anyone can read it with a Bluetooth app on a phone and broadcast the same address, and bringing it near your PC could fool BleUnlock into unlocking. Devices with an IRK are not exposed this way, because the IRK never appears in broadcasts. Recommended: use it only in a trusted place such as home, or leave the password empty under "Credentials" so the PC only locks when you leave and never unlocks automatically.

data.name: Config_SuddenGuardHint
data.value: A jump in the signal is not trusted straight away: a sudden drop while unlocked shows no prompt and locks only if it lasts; a sudden rise after locking unlocks only once it is steady. Gradual changes follow the normal rules.

data.name: Config_SuddenReferenceHint
data.value: Compared with the average of up to this many readings actually sent by the device in the last 120 s before the trigger (repeated samples excluded). With fewer than 5, no sudden-change check. 5–50.

data.name: Config_SuddenDeltaHint
data.value: A trigger this far from the reference average counts as a sudden jump. 0 = protection off. 0 or 5–60.

data.name: Config_SuddenDropSecondsHint
data.value: After a sudden drop, no prompt: if within this time at least 3 real readings are all below the lock threshold, the screen locks directly; one reading back above cancels it. 5–300 s.

data.name: Config_SuddenRiseSecondsHint
data.value: After a sudden rise while locked: unlocks only if within this time at least 2 real readings are all above the unlock threshold; a fall or too few readings means no unlock. 1–60 s.

data.name: Rules_GuardNote
data.value: Sudden-change protection: when a trigger is ≥ {1} dB from the average of up to {0} previous real readings, a drop is watched for {2} s (at least 3 real readings all below the lock threshold lock the screen directly, with no prompt) and a rise for {3} s (at least 2 real readings all above the unlock threshold unlock); the reading-count rules below apply to gradual changes.
